AcquireSourceArgs.description:
Acquire a REE source from an origin or a staged upload.

An REE holds at most one source, and acquisition is only legal into an
empty slot. There is no replace: a source already there is the author's,
and giving it up is a separate act they perform with ``remove_source``.
Acquiring into an occupied slot is a precondition failure, never a reset —
a reset here would erase every condition the acquisition could refuse on,
which is exactly how a sealed REE used to get silently unsealed.

origin_url.title: Origin Url

ExecUploadRequest.description:
Bundle the REE and upload the bundle as a file.

For output too large for the control socket: the workbench writes ``ree bundle``'s
stdout to a file in the bench, then sends that file over HTTP — ``PUT`` to
``transfer_path`` on the same address it dialed for this socket, so the workbench
still only ever dials out — and answers ``done`` once the control plane has taken
it. Bulk bytes never share the socket that carries keepalive pings and every other
request.

``transfer_path`` is an absolute path naming a single-use transfer the
control plane opened for this request; it is the transfer's only credential.
ExecUploadRequest.title: ExecUploadRequest

Failure.description:
Machine-readable description of why an action did not succeed.

A single shared object carried on every ``failed`` :class:`ActionResult`
(and, over time, through error frames, run records, and HTTP envelopes). The
contract is that a component *enriches* the same failure as it travels up
the layers rather than collapsing it to ``str(exc)`` at each hop, so the
``category``/``origin`` a client sees are the ones the originating component
chose.

``transfer_path`` on the address it dialed for this socket, lands the file,
and answers ``done``. ``transfer_path`` names a single-use transfer the
control plane opened for this request; it is the transfer's only credential.
FetchFileRequest.title: FetchFileRequest

reviewer who cares about one experiment should not have to sit through the
others. Running them all is the caller issuing this command in sequence.

No ``basis``, for the same reason activation takes none: the experiment runs
in the workspace the build left behind and inherits what that evidence is
worth.

VenvExperimentEnvironmentContract.description:
A packed Python virtual environment as the experiment environment substrate.

The build packs the venv as a gzipped tarball at ``artifact_path``; a
runnable restores it to ``venv_restore_dir`` (an absolute path, because a
venv bakes absolute paths and must be restored where it was built) and runs
the command with that venv's ``bin`` on ``PATH``. There is no image ref: the
workbench base image is the environment. ``venv_restore_dir`` defaults to the
path a repo2ree build packs; an inspected artifact overrides it with the path
recovered from the venv's own ``pyvenv.cfg``.
VenvExperimentEnvironmentContract.title: VenvExperimentEnvironmentContract

WorkbenchHello.description:

and additive — new fields must default so an older workbench still parses,
and unknown fields are *ignored* (unlike the frames) so an older control
plane still accepts a newer workbench's hello.
